statements.text: I'm eager to hear from our witnesses whether Congress can properly regulate AI, while allowing the innovation to flourish.
statements.venue: Hearing remarks, as quoted on PoliticalQuotes

statements.text: This is something that is going to sneak up on us, and we'll get to the point where we're in too deep to really make meaningful changes before it's too late.

I am worried about being pulled over and questioned by a robot someday. I don't want to live in a society where a task of government that should be fulfilled by real life people are being replaced with AI. [...] That's very scary to me, and I think we need to be very cautious.

I don't want the Chinese to be developing the next turn of the century model that's going to change our lives. But I want to make sure that we all are on the same page as Americans, as a society, and that we are very cautious with what we get behind.

AI czar. 
Border czar.
Voting czar.
Space czar.

Kamala Harris is the czar of everything, but has accomplished nothing.

It seems as if, as this develops, we'd like to perhaps see more transparency in the process. Is it unrealistic to think that the songwriters, the people, the American people, whoever, could kind of see what goes into these sources of what has an influence on the AI.
statements.context: House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI and copyright interoperability, where Rep. Gooden questions a witness about transparency into AI training data.

statements.text: Thank you. Ms. Melugin, the Biden Administration passed sweeping Executive Orders on AI which weren't authorized by any congressional action or directive. Do you think the previous administration bypassed Congress and micromanaged AI development without public accountability?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI innovation and competition, questioning a witness about executive branch authority over AI policy.

statements.text: [...] as a trend it seems like every State is jumping to regulate AI, and perhaps some of them are doing it just to show early participation, do you think that is well thought out? [...] what are the long term effects of having a decentralized patchwork of laws, how does this help or hinder new entrants?
statements.context: House hearing titled 'AI at a Crossroads: A Nationwide Strategy or Californication?' where a member questions a witness about state-level AI regulation.

statements.text:
America leads or America loses. It is that simple.

The Trump Administration's Genesis Mission unleashes American innovation in AI, energy, and next generation technology.

This is how the United States will continue to LEAD the world!

https://t.co/9nognaILk1

When Washington talks about artificial intelligence, the conversation is about chatbots, deepfakes, and misinformation. Those debates matter. But while policymakers are still focused on what AI can say, the technology has transitioned into its next phase. [...] We are now entering the age of agentic AI, and Congress is not ready.

China and Russia don’t need to beat America in AI if they can convince Americans to sabotage our own innovation.

I’m calling on @DAGToddBlanche to investigate foreign influence behind the fight against data centers.

https://t.co/xFFAN8oeQa

Artificial intelligence will shape the future of our economy, national security, and global competitiveness. The United States cannot allow foreign adversaries to manipulate our AI policy and compromise our leadership on this technology.

statements.text:
China has infiltrated the American AI debate and is rolling out a massive propaganda machine to stall our progress. 

That’s why I’m working with @AGToddBlance to root out all CCP manipulation of American AI policy—so we don’t cede global leadership of this technology to Beijing. https://t.co/5vHEnR0CNW
statements.quoted:
The X Safety team conducted an investigation into suspected Chinese inauthentic accounts involved in influence operations:

We identified a bot farm of approximately 200,000 accounts. Within this farm, we found 200 accounts posting in a manner that could manipulate a legitimate debate about American AI and energy policy.

These posts contained claims that AI data centers are driving up household electricity prices and straining the grid. Others included AI-generated cartoons that depicted data-center operators enriching themselves at the public's expense.

We remain committed to maintaining an open and authentic platform where people debate topics of public interest. We take seriously any attempts to undermine the integrity of the global town square and suspend accounts that violate our Authenticity policy.

statements.text: As agentic AI becomes more powerful, China and other adversaries will look for every weakness they can exploit. Congress needs to know whether our current defenses are able to keep pace and where we need to act before the next threat becomes a crisis.
statements.venue: Press release on letter to DNI Clayton
